Treat the previous unresolved coordinate list as inconclusive, not as evidence against this rule.', 2), ('arc_task_d4c70c99_mark_matching_colors_across_separator', 'ARC task-d4c70c99: mark matching colors across separator', 'For recurring task-d4c70c99, the grid has two equal-sized panels separated by a single uniform divider (vertical or horizontal). Find the color value occurring in both panels; output a panel-sized grid filled with that shared color, and put 3 wherever both corresponding cells have the shared color. A solved test used shared 7 and output 12x13, with 3 at aligned 7/7 cells. Another solved test was 10x25 with vertical divider 4 at column 13 (1-based), panels 10x12, shared color 0; output had 3 at 1-based positions (2,4), (3,8), (4,3), (4,9), (4,11), (5,1), (5,2), (5,6), (5,8), (5,10), (6,2), (9,6), (10,12), and 0 elsewhere. Critical: parse each row into exact widths and compare same relative coordinates. A wrong first attempt came from manually misreading right-panel zero positions in rows 3 and 8; splitting at the divider and calculating programmatically avoided this.', 3), ('arc_task_4b1f4f06_shifted_edge_rails_project_marker_rays', 'ARC task-4b1f4f06: shifted edge rails project marker rays', "For recurring ARC task-4b1f4f06, two equal-color rail segments lie on opposite parallel grid edges, shifted along the edge direction; isolated markers are in the rail color (or another foreground color) on one active rail's coordinate range. Let d be the signed translation from the source-side rail segment to its opposite segment. For each marker, replace the marker with 4. Extend a source-side ray from the marker toward its own edge rail, in the marker's original color, stopping before the rail. Translate its coordinate along the rail axis by d and draw a full perpendicular line across the grid at that translated coordinate in the marker color, preserving any rail cells it crosses. Important: projected lines include boundary cells wherever those cells are not part of an edge rail; do not restrict them to columns/rows 1..N-2. A first test answer omitted col 0 from projected horizontal lines and was wrong.

Confirmed demo 1 (18x24, background 3): top rail color 1 at row 0, cols 0..6; bottom rail at row 17, cols 14..20 (offset +14). Color-5 markers at (9,14),(13,15),(13,16),(14,20),(15,18). Each marker becomes 4; rays extend downward to row 16 at original columns; full projected vertical 5-lines run rows 1..16 at columns 0,1,2,4,6 (translated c-14), including col 0; edge-rail cells remain unchanged.

Confirmed demo 2 (22x15, background 9): top rail color 2 at row 0, cols 0..2; bottom rail at row 21, cols 5..7 (offset +5). Color-8 markers at (13,7),(17,5),(19,6). Each becomes 4; source rays extend downward to row 20 at original columns; projected full vertical lines run rows 1..20 at columns 2,0,1, including boundary cols when not rail cells. Preserve rails.

Confirmed test on this instance (background 8): left rail color 9 at col 0 rows 4..11 and right rail at col 26 rows 13..20, offset +9. Color-3 markers at (4,17),(6,21),(7,2),(9,22),(10,5),(11,17). Markers become 4; source rays go left toward col 0, stopping at col 1; projected full horizontal 3-lines are at rows 13,15,16,18,19,20 across cols 0..25, preserving right-edge 9 cells at col 26. Use zero-based coordinates. Both source rays and projected lines are needed; preserve existing edge rail cells, but fill unrailed boundary cells on projected lines.

Confirmed another test on task-4b1f4f06: 5x17, background 9; top rail color 6 at row 0, cols 0..7; bottom rail at row 4, cols 9..16 (offset +9). Interior color-1 markers at (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(2,7),(3,0),(3,1),(3,6). Each marker becomes 4. For each, fill the vertical source ray toward top rail with 1 (rows 1 up to just before the marker). Translate each marker column +9 and draw a full vertical 1-line at that target column through non-rail cells, rows 0..3; preserve both rails and background elsewhere. This confirms source ray + full translated projection, including unrailed opposite boundary cells. Answer was correct.", 5), ('arc_task_82d6b2bb_complete_repeating_pattern_through_zeros', 'ARC task-82d6b2bb: complete sparse periodic color patterns', 'Task-82d6b2bb is to complete a periodic color pattern through zeros. Infer the shortest consistent period and its coordinate/orientation from colored cells; fill every cell, not just zeros, using the periodic mapping. For down-right diagonal bands, color depends on d=(c-r) mod p; each observed monochrome band gives the color for that residue. Solved example: p=5 with residues 0→1, 1→3, 2→5, 3→6, 4→9, so every output cell is [1,3,5,6,9][(c-r)%5]. Observations were 1 on d=-5, 3 on d=-4, 9 on d=-1, 6 on d=3, and 5 on d=7. Other verified example: a 14x14 input with down-right bands of colors 1,4,5,8 had p=4 and residue map (c-r)%4: 0→8, 1→5, 2→4, 3→1; output is a full diagonal periodic tile. If stripes are down-left use r+c instead. Horizontal full-row stripes are a special case of periodic completion; infer period and phase from observed row indices, then repeat. Prior demos: rows [0,4,2,9] became [9,4,2,9] (period 3); a stripe sequence with period 7 filled blank rows to match the repeating cycle. Do not assume zeros are background; use all clues to resolve period, axis and phase.', 2), ('arc_task_3b58a624_recolor_matching_component_to_l_template_color', 'ARC task-3b58a624: recolor one object to prominent L color', 'For recurring Continual-ARC task-3b58a624, each demo preserves the grid and recolors one separate object (occasionally a cell/endpoint) to the color of a prominent L-shaped component. D5 bg2: color1 horizontal triplet row8 cols12–14 becomes8; reference L color8. D6 bg9: singleton2 at (7,6) becomes1; reference L color1. D7 bg6: lower color9 triplet row9 cols2–4 becomes3; reference L color3. D8 bg8: vertical color3 triplet rows0–2 col7 becomes4; reference L color4. Earlier solved instance from prior memory: 29x18, bg4, prominent L color7; recolor only the 5-cell color3 component at rows12–13 cols11–13 to7; identical 5-cell color3 component near lower-right stays unchanged.
